sources.title: A brutal sell-off for AI stocks sends Wall Street reeling (KY3/AP, 2026-11-05)
Wall St rallies after last week's AI rout; Nvidia falls (Detroit News, 2026-11-09)
Stock Market Today: Nvidia Pressures Indexes (24/7 Wall St, 2026-11-09)
NVIDIA Sets Conference Call for Third-Quarter Financial Results
LLY stock jumps as Q3 earnings beat estimates, 2026 sales view raised (Zacks)

market_view: Last week AI stocks sold off hard. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4%, its worst day since April 2025, on worries that higher borrowing costs and political pushback after the midterms will slow data-center spending. Today's rebound is led by chip stocks and cheaper oil, while Nvidia is down on a board probe of its CEO. The market still looks stressed: VIX around 25, high-yield bonds lagging Treasuries, and breadth mixed. Investors are moving out of AI and high-momentum stocks into health care, staples, payment networks and Treasuries. On this first day I'm proposing a small defensive set of picks that don't depend on AI spending, and I'm not chasing the chip bounce ahead of tomorrow's CPI and Nvidia's Nov 17 report.
key_drivers: 2026-11-05: S&P 500 -4.4%, Nasdaq -5.5% in an AI sell-off (AMD -17%, NVDA -9%), driven by rate and data-center politics fears after the midterms
2026-11-09: Broad rebound as oil falls and chips bounce; VIX dips intraday but is still about 25; Nvidia lags on a board inquiry into CEO Huang
2026-11-10: October CPI due, consensus about 2.7% y/y; a hot number would hit rate-sensitive AI names again
2026-11-17: Nvidia FQ3 results after the close, a key test for the AI capex story
2026-10-29: Lilly Q3 revenue +39%, 2026 sales guidance raised to $91-92B; health care (XLV) is up 8.5% over 20 days
Market health is 'stressed': HYG has lagged IEF by 2.2% over 20 days, and IEF is +2.9% over 20 days as yields fall

positions.thesis: Earnings are growing fast and don't depend on AI spending. Q3 revenue rose 39%, 2026 guidance was raised by about $5.5B, and the obesity pipeline keeps adding wins (Foundayo, retatrutide). The stock is 27% above its 200-day average, so it is a strong-trend big company that rotation out of AI favours. This is a weeks-long hold, not a trade.
positions.exit_plan: Sell if the obesity-drug thesis breaks (pricing or policy shock, a pipeline failure), if price closes below the 200-day average, or on the trailing stop. Review before the early-Feb 2027 earnings.
positions.plain_reason: Its weight-loss drugs keep selling much faster than expected.

positions.thesis: A high-quality payment network with steady earnings that keeps compounding, in an uptrend (22% above its 200-day average). It holds up well when investors rotate out of AI, and nothing changes in its business before late-January earnings. The next date (Jan 28, 2027) comes from third-party calendars and is not confirmed by Visa.
positions.exit_plan: Sell on a consumer-spending downturn signal, regulatory action on fees, a close below the 200-day average, or the trailing stop.
positions.plain_reason: It earns a small fee on every card purchase, steady in shaky markets.

positions.thesis: Health care is the sector the current rotation favours: low AI exposure, defensive earnings, and a strong trend (+8.5% over 20 days, 17.6% above its 200-day average). This bet is about the sector itself, not just more S&P 500 exposure.
signals: Defensive sector in a stressed tape
positions.exit_plan: Sell if the market mood turns healthy and money rotates back into growth, if drug-pricing policy turns hostile, or if price closes below the 50-day average.
positions.plain_reason: Health care companies keep earning money even when the economy wobbles.

positions.thesis: A hedge against more equity stress and falling real yields. Gold miners are +14.7% this week, which suggests gold is building momentum again after its pullback.
positions.exit_plan: Sell if the mood normalises and yields rise sharply, or on the 20% trailing stop.
positions.plain_reason: Gold often holds value when stocks get scary.

positions.thesis: Treasuries are rising (+2.9% over 20 days) while credit spreads widen. They offset equity risk if the AI unwind spreads into the wider economy.
positions.exit_plan: Sell if CPI comes in hot and yields jump, or once stress gauges return to healthy.
positions.plain_reason: Government bonds usually rise when stocks fall.

plain_summary: Mostly S&P 500, plus small bets on health care, payments, gold and government bonds while markets are nervous.
upcoming_events: 2026-11-10: October CPI (consensus about 2.7% y/y). A hot reading would hurt rate-sensitive tech and bonds.
2026-11-13: October PPI, another inflation read that feeds Fed expectations.
2026-11-17 (after close): Nvidia FQ3 FY27 earnings, the key test for AI spending; NVDA is also under a board probe.
About 2026-11-17 to 11-19: Home Depot, Walmart and other retailers report (watch consumer health).
Ongoing: political fallout from the midterms over data-center power costs and permits.
watchlist: MA (second payment network; add if V works)
MSFT (big company that fell on AI fears; watch after NVDA earnings)
AMD / SMH (only if the AI capex thesis is confirmed after NVDA on 11/17)

plain_summary: The market is bouncing today, but none of the stocks that fell looked like a clean overreaction, so I'm buying nothing this hour; there's also no important news about SPY, the only thing we own.
